title: Tree hit shake and falling trees
player_outcome: Trees shudder on every axe hit, then topple over away from you with a thud and a burst of leaves and wood, instead of vanishing.
design: Verified: tile objects render as one MultiMesh per chunk and model variant (TileObjectRenderer.cs:90-117); trees disappear on removal.
TileObjectRenderer.Rebuild records Dictionary<long objId, (MultiMesh mm, int index, Transform3D xf)>. HideInstance(obj) sets a zero-scale transform; ShowInstance restores it.

New game/World/TreeEffects.cs (pooled, max 3 wobbles + 3 falls). On ObjectHit Damaged for objects with SizeY ≥ 4: hide the instance and show a pooled MeshInstance3D copy (PropLibrary.Model(ObjectModel(def, variant), multimesh:false)). It wobbles ±3° about the base, damped, for 0.18 s, then the instance is restored.
On ObjectHit Broken with Def.Topple: the chunk rebuild removes the tree. Spawn a falling copy that rotates 90° about the base edge away from the player over 0.9 s (ease-in).
On impact: 'tree_fall' thud, EffectKit Leaves ×30 + wood chips ×20 along the trunk line, CameraShake.Kick(0.1) if within 12 m, then sink and fade over 0.3 s.
Pre-load non-multimesh tree meshes for all tree defs at world start (no hitch on the first chop).
tests: Smoke basic.cmds (tree section from P3-21): 'assert errors == 0' after the tree falls (wait 2)
verification: Timescale screenshots of wobble and fall (lavapipe)
perf: gd.objects p95 unchanged; no main-thread load on the first chop (perf report max frame)
risks: A chunk rebuild during a wobble re-creates the MultiMesh; re-apply hidden indices after Rebuild.
P1's lag work may change TileObjectRenderer rebuild budgeting; rebase.
